rule_0.statement: THE STAND-FIRST HOLD (wave 33). The wave-32 mined face: at the sixth exchange (the L fires 211, the R the sole carrier) the R's share hit 0 at tick 215 -- five ticks BEFORE the L's band entry (220) -- and the R's pads left the band at 216 (the fold re-formed), stranding the R when the L's completion opened its fire window at 220; one-legged on the L from 216, the positional-correction budget refused at 300. The wave-32 deadline reads the other's LAST TD and clause (a) never yields mid-glide, so no fire deadline can cover a carrier that unloads mid-swing BY STRUCTURE -- the wave-32 bank. THIS WAVE'S LAW IS THE MIRROR: not a fire deadline but a PAD HOLD -- the CARRIER's pads are held AT THE FLOOR while the swing's own stall runs, so the unload (the share's vanish) cannot lift them, and the wave-32 exchange fire lands on live pads at the completion exactly as shipped. THREE PARTS. (1) THE MECHANISM, MINED on the wave-32 shipped trace's first walk run (the byte-exact cf382756 reproduction, the declared script .tmp/w33_receipt/mine_carrier.py, the decision rule fixed in the script header BEFORE the numbers were recorded): (i) THE STALL -- the first three swings lifted really (the lift-first hold released at 99/143/161 with hold counts 2/1/1 and the arch peaks 1.5212 mm @102 / 13.1310 mm @150 / 7.8885 mm @167); from the L@175 fire on, EVERY swing STALLED -- the hold NEVER released (hold count 9 = the whole swing, release tick None) and the arch peak read 0.0087-0.0124 mm -- the fired pads never left the touch band: they CREEPED in-band, dragging (the swing-start slip series 0.1009-0.7674 m/s, worst @193). (ii) THE CAUSE -- the exchange fires land on pads STILL LOADED (the fired leg's rxn at its own fire: 2.265 N @175, 2.156 @184, 0.492 @193, 5.455 @202, 4.649 @211 -- vs 0.000 at the three real lifts): the +1 class's load transfer has not finished when the clock fires, a loaded pad cannot lift, the stall. (iii) THE CONTROL -- the carriers of cycles 2-5 NEVER read rxn 0 (the L's series 23.403-36.763 N [175,184); 2.327-4.760 [184,193); 5.675-15.744 [193,202); 6.492-40.904 [202,211)): the unload struck ONLY the cycle-6 carrier (the R's 4.025 @211 -> 2.769 @213 -> 0.558 @214 -> 0.000 @215, its pair-min 9.63 um @214 -> 193.72 um @215 post-tick = the 216 tick-start: the wave-30 unload-lift face). (2) THE LAW, SHIPPED (gait_controller.hpp): THE CARRIER'S STAND-FIRST HOLD -- while the OTHER hind is mid-glide (mode 1) AND ITS OWN PER-SWING STALL CLOCK has run the arch's back half (the new hind_step_stall_[o] counter, incremented by the existing lift-first hold's held branch and reset at each fire, reading hind_step_stall_[o] >= tair - tair/2 - kUnloadTicks = 9 - 4 - 1 = 4) AND this leg is the ride-era carrier (hind_step_last_td_[hl] != 0, the wave-32 arming letter) with live pads (touching_prev_[hl]), this leg's STANCE TARGET IS REPLACED by the IK hold at the pad spots captured at the arm tick -- the same whole-branch replacement the wave-29 glide hold makes (the designed stance tables AND the wave-27 feed-forward both displaced), so the unloaded columns cannot lift the pad (the wave-30 face disarmed BY STRUCTURE); the hold releases when the other completes (mode 0) -- the wave-32 exchange fire then lands on live pads at the completion, untouched. Clause (a) NEVER yields -- untouched. Zero new numeric constants: tair is the machinery's own air time, tair/2 the arch's own half, kUnloadTicks=1 the wave-32 mined +1 class, kTouch/kReleaseBand reach the law only through the existing hold counter. The MAPPED lead: the mined strand had the arm signal present at the 215 decision (the L's stall count 4 at 215 = the threshold) exactly one decision before the fold's first band-exit read (216) -- the +1 class AGAIN: the hold arms kUnloadTicks ahead of the lift. On the shipped bytes the law first engages at the 179 decision (the L@175 stall's fourth in-band held tick), pinning the cycle-2 carrier R for [179,184) -- the first divergence IS the law's engagement. (3) THE INTERACTION: the pin is not a fire and moves no fire; the exchange calendar's letters (every fire ON the other's completion tick, the completions at band entries in [fire+9,fire+30], the strict alternation, the (b)-waive) are carried unchanged; the strand era is consumed -- at 220 the R fires ON the L's completion with live pads (the R fired at rxn~0 for the first time since 160: a real lift is the likely class, the R@160 real swing took +15, the stalled class took +9 -- both inside the window). THE PREDICTED CALENDAR: the fence bytes through 178 are IDENTICAL; the FIRST DIVERGENCE EXACTLY TICK 179; the fire chain continues past 211 for the first time (R@220, then the exchange continues: the L fires on the R's completion, point chain 220(R), then +9 or +15 spans compounding -- the point estimate for the R's 220-replant completion 235 (+15, the real-lift class), the L's fire there). THE SUPPORT: the touching-class exchange-era sub-2 ticks SHRINK vs the wave-32's 70 (the pinned R counts DOWN through [215,220) where it lifted before) but do NOT empty (the fores' collapse is the carried cause) -- the contact-class shrinks vs 68 likewise.
